newsitem.title: USA: USDA expands Medfly quarantine area in Florida.
newsitem.headline: USDA expands Medfly quarantine area in Florida.

text.p: The Agriculture Department on Thursday expanded the quarantine area in central Florida to prevent the spread of the destructive Mediterranean fruit fly.

USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said in a Federal Register notice that the quarantined area now includes portions of Manatee and Polk counties, plus an additional area of Hillsborough County. The area is on Florida's west coast, near Tampa.
The Mediterranean fruit fly, known to scientiests as Ceratitis capitata, is one of the world's most destructive pests of numerous fruits and vegetables and can cause heavy losses of crops.
Three weeks ago, the USDA added a portion of Hillsborough County to the quarantined area after trapping surveys showed the pest had spread.
